scenes.scene: Extreme close-up insert shot of hands and objects only; no face is visible anywhere in the frame. Setting: Babuji's small dark room at night in an old village house: an iron bed, whitewashed walls, a hanging lantern giving warm light. What happens: Extreme close-up of an old woman's wrinkled hands only, in a white saree, unfolding a folded letter whose writing cannot be read; her face is not in the shot. Nobody speaks and nobody's lips move; no voices at all. There are no people, no faces and no heads anywhere in this shot, only what is described. Nobody looks into the camera lens: the camera is an invisible observer that nobody notices. Everyone is clearly Indian, with brown skin and Indian features, like real actors in an Indian TV serial; never cartoon, anime or plastic-looking. Film look: Photorealistic live-action Indian feature film set in a North Indian village, shot on a cinema camera with anamorphic lenses, warm natural light, monsoon atmosphere, natural skin texture, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain. Upright, normal orientation (never rotated or upside down). Widescreen 16:9 cinematic film frame, composed like a feature film, faces at eye level. No text, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no signboards, no shop signs, no posters, no name plates, no vehicle number plates, no readable letters anywhere.
scenes.sound: Soft emotional music, no other voices, and an off-screen narrator's voice-over: Babuji's voice: a gentle, slow, slightly raspy old Indian man's voice, speaking Hindi warmly and playfully, close to the microphone.
